name: Rain
label: Dischord
lede: A second-wave Revolution Summer band that lasted about a year, cut six songs with Ian MacKaye, broke up, and then got released three years later by a guy from Fugazi.

eras.title: The second wave shows up
eras.text: Revolution Summer had turned DC hardcore inward and melodic the year before, and a younger set of bands took the hint. Rain was one of them: a trio with scene veteran Bert Queiroz on bass and Jon Kirschten and Eli Janney in their first real band.

years.src: Dischord · Some Will Never Know · Wikipedia · Exclaim!
years.h: Jon Kirschten, Bert Queiroz, Eli Janney: Rain starts as a trio
years.p: Jon Kirschten sings and plays guitar, [[Bert Queiroz|d657171b-961c-4078-ab84-90b2c69f0095]] plays bass, [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] plays drums. Dischord files them as a key band in the second wave of Revolution Summer.
years.xp:
Queiroz was the old hand: he'd already come through the Untouchables, [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]], Double O and Second Wind. For Janney and Kirschten, Rain was the first proper band, though Kirschten had passed briefly through [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]].

The sound followed the path [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] had cut: melodic, introspective, still loud. Reviewers would later throw in [[Mission of Burma|db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e]] and early R.E.M. as reference points.

eras.title: Two sessions and out
eras.text: Rain's whole recorded life happened in one year and two studios. By the time the Inner Ear tapes were done, so was the band.

years.h: Rain's demo at WGNS with Geoff Turner
years.p: Rain cut a four-song demo tape at WGNS, the studio run by [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]]'s [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]]. One song, In Rain, never made it onto the later record.

years.h: Soulside's Scott McCloud joins Rain on second guitar
years.p: [[Scott McCloud|11e1e118-8744-45f0-9c37-dc4944541134]], already the guitarist in [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]], joins Rain as second guitarist and singer before their Inner Ear session.

years.h: Rain break up with the Inner Ear tapes unreleased
years.p: Dischord dates Rain's end to 1987, shortly after the Inner Ear session with Ian MacKaye. Nothing has been released yet.

eras.title: Released by a friend
eras.text: Rain was gone, but the songs kept surfacing, first on a Dischord compilation, then on a 12" from Guy Picciotto's own label, Peterbilt. Meanwhile Scott McCloud and Eli Janney had started Girls Against Boys.

years.h: Scott McCloud and Eli Janney start Girls Against Boys
years.p: Rain drummer Eli Janney and second guitarist Scott McCloud form [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]], which outlasts Rain by decades and lands on a major label in the '90s.

years.h: Rain's Worlds At War on State of the Union · Dischord No. 32
years.p: Dischord puts one Rain song on its 1989 DC compilation, the first time most people outside town hear the band.

years.h: La Vache Qui Rit: Rain's 1987 session, out three years late
years.p: Rain recorded these six songs at Inner Ear Studios in 1987 with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] producing, then broke up. [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]]'s Peterbilt label put them out as a 12" in 1990.
years.xp:
The title is the French cheese with the laughing cow. Six songs: That Time Of Year, End Of My Mind, Snakeout, Worlds At War, Around The Axis and Rivers. It stayed out of print for most of the next two decades.

Dischord says Rain recorded twice in 1987, first at WGNS, then at Inner Ear with MacKaye. The Some Will Never Know archive counts five songs from the MacKaye session; the 12" carries six, all described by Dischord's Bandcamp as recorded in 1987.

eras.title: The cow laughs again
eras.text: Dischord and Peterbilt brought the record back on CD, and a band most people knew only as a footnote to Girls Against Boys got reviewed like a new release.

years.cap: La Vache Qui Rit, Dischord/Peterbilt CD reissue
years.h: Rain's La Vache Qui Rit reissued on CD
years.p: Out of print for years, Rain's only record returns on CD from Dischord and Peterbilt, remastered.
years.xp: Exclaim! heard Rites of Spring, Mission of Burma and early R.E.M. in it. Exclaim!'s Vish Khanna praised the band's "edgy melodicism" and a poppy streak running under the frantic parts. The record now lives on Dischord's Bandcamp alongside the rest of the catalog.

years.p: Eli Janney and Scott McCloud: [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]]. Bert Queiroz: Manifesto, then [[Thunderball|8579d918-835b-4c1d-ac00-45a7f4a8763a]]. Jon Kirschten: The Chris Bald 96, Special K and Las Mordidas.
